hints: Compare "2.10.0" and "2.9.3" the way Python compares two strings: one character at a time, left to right, stopping at the first difference. Which characters decide it, and is that what a version number means?
The likely mistake is comparing versions as text. Each part between the dots is a number of its own, and the parts count from left to right: major first, then minor, then patch.
solution_explanation: Split each version on the dots and turn every part into an int, so "2.10.0" becomes [2, 10, 0]. Python compares two lists item by item from the left, which is exactly the major, then minor, then patch order semantic versioning uses, and 10 is bigger than 9 as a number.
